title: The Future of Qwen: A Generalist Agent Model — Junyang Lin, Alibaba Qwen
talk_summary: Junyang Lin presents Qwen3 model family (MoE and dense sizes, hybrid thinking/non-thinking modes, dynamic thinking budgets, MCP/tool-use during reasoning) and Qwen's roadmap toward generalist agent models trained with RL and environment feedback.

takeaways.what_they_do: A single model supports a configurable max thinking-token budget; they show accuracy rises with budget, so you set the smallest budget that meets your target accuracy instead of always maxing reasoning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you have a large thinking budget like 32,000 tokens you can even achieve more than 80
takeaways.numbers: AIME24: ~40% at small budget vs >80% at 32k thinking tokens; >95% accuracy achievable at 8k budget in their example

takeaways.what_they_do: One model can run in thinking or non-thinking mode selected by prompt or hyperparameter, so trivial tasks skip reasoning entirely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can use prompts or hyperparameters to control its behaviors as you like

takeaways.what_they_do: Model thinks, calls a tool, ingests environment feedback, and continues thinking in one loop rather than a single plan-then-act pass.
They measure task accuracy across increasing thinking budgets to find the point of diminishing returns.
They plan to scale context to 1M+ tokens to support memory and long-horizon agent runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're going to scale the context at least 1 million tokens this year for most of our models
